== Biography ==
George was born about 1769. He is the son of [[Glasgow-1120|James Glasgow]] and [[Scott-41785|Mary Scott]]. 


* Fact: Christening (7 May 1769)  Wandell and Lamington, Lanarkshire, Scotland

=== Possible George Glasgow, Royal Artillery reports, 1771–1795 ===
A Royal Regiment of Artillery promotion report names Second Lieutenant George Glasgow to be First Lieutenant in the room of Francis Downman, preferred.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395686209/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1771-09-07, p.1].</ref>

An Office of Ordnance notice names Captain-Lieutenant George Glasgow to be Captain in the Royal Regiment of Artillery, vice Wright.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395737286/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1793-10-05, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/257580089/ The Observer, 1793-10-06, p.1].</ref>

A War Office notice dated 15 May 1795 names Captain George Glasgow, artillery, among captains appointed to be majors in the army.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395709939/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1795-05-21, p.2].</ref>

The shared name, artillery service and progressive ranks make one career plausible. Personal continuity across the twenty-two years is unproved. The 1795 notice announces promotion to majors in the army; it does not itself name a family or establish a technical brevet designation.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1529]]. Estimated c. 1769 birth would make him too young for 1771 if approximately correct; the 1793/1795 Captain/Major notices could fit by age. A later namesake remains possible, without a service identifier.

=== Possible George Glasgow, unassigned Second Lieutenant appointment, 1774 ===
George Glasgow, gentleman, is reported appointed Second Lieutenant, vice Second Lieutenant Barnes, promoted.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395693121/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1774-09-24, p.2].</ref>

No regiment is stated in the appointment paragraph. It cannot safely be joined to the George Glasgow already reported as an artillery first lieutenant in 1771; the lower rank is not evidence of a demotion.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1529]]. Estimated c. 1769 birth would make him about five in 1774 if approximately correct, a strong chronology tension. Estimate not independently checked; weak/unlikely lead.
